One woman wey dey 22 years don born for our hospital three days ago. Today she carry her newborn pikin come for routine immunization. As dem reach, she tell us say di pikin no gree suck breast at all. Di pikin too dey weak, e dey sleep pass normal, and e no dey wake well.

She talk say anytime she try put breast for di pikin mouth, e no go suck at all. She come notice say di pikin hand, leg, and whole body dey very cold, like ice. Di body too cold reach where she dey fear to touch di pikin with her bare hand, and na only when she wrap plenty cloth before she fit carry am.

She talk say di pikin no dey suck breast, di whole body dey cold to touch, and di pikin don dey more weak as time dey go. E no fit move hand, e no fit stretch leg, e no get normal movement or reflex. Na so e just dey lie down, no strength, no movement. She talk say anybody wey look di pikin go know say di pikin really sick and don tire.

Wetin fit cause this kain thing? Wetin una think say fit happen make pikin body dey this kind freezing cold? Na only because di pikin no dey suck breast, abi another problem fit dey cause am too? Wetin fit be di treatment wey make di pikin begin suck breast again?

Also, concerning di immunization wey dem suppose give di pikin today, wetin be una professional advice?
column19: Dis pikin get severe neonatal sepsis or possible meningitis wey cause severe hypoglycemia, hypothermia, and floppiness; di cold body na sign of severe infection and metabolic collapse, no be only because e no suck breast. Immediate treatment na: warm di pikin with skin-to-skin or incubator, check blood sugar and give 10% dextrose IV stat, start IV antibiotics (Ampicillin plus Gentamicin or Cefotaxime) immediately, give Vitamin K 1mg IM, and admit for close monitoring. Do NOT give immunization today—defer until pikin stable and well for at least 48 hours. Counsel mother on danger signs and exclusive breastfeeding once pikin recover. Refer to higher facility if no improvement in 24 hours or if convulsions start.

**Wetin you fit do:**
1. **See mental health professional** (like child psychologist or counselor) na correct step—dem go help di pikin talk about im feelings and process di grief for healthy way; if una hospital get, ask for referral.
2. **For food and play:** No force am chop, but make you dey offer small small food wey e like, chop together with am, and gently invite am play without pressure—patience and love plenty na key.

**About medicine:** For now, na counseling and family support na di main treatment; medicine like antidepressant no dey usually necessary for grief unless doctor check am well and see say di depression heavy well-well (like if e no dey sleep, dey talk say e wan die, or e dey lose weight bad-bad). Wetin fit cause this strong pain and plenty bleeding for 7-month pregnant woman na condition wey placenta pull comot from womb wall before time (Placental Abruption) or placenta dey block womb door (Placenta Previa).

The first thing to do now na to rush her quickly to a standard hospital make dem put her on IV drip, oxygen, and monitor her heart-beat because delay fit cause death.

Doctors go run urgent tests like Ultrasound scan to see the baby and placenta, and blood tests like PCV (to check blood level) and Blood Grouping for crossmatch.

The best treatment for this emergency na urgent delivery (mostly by Caesarean Section/Operation) and blood transfusion to replace the blood wey she lose.

To keep body clean and safe, make pregnant women avoid raw/half-cooked meat and eggs, drink clean water, wash hands always, and wipe from front to back after using toilet to prevent infection.

One pregnant woman come our hospital this morning. As she reach, she dey feel serious pain. She dey cry well well as she hold her back and belle because of the pain.

After about 8 to 10 minutes wey we carry am enter labour ward, we examine am and see say the baby don already dey come out and her cervix don open finish. Not long after, she born one baby girl.

After delivery, we do all the necessary care for both the mama and the baby. Later, we carry both of them go one room make dem rest.

After some time, the woman call us come say her body dey very weak, she dey tire well well, and her eye dey somehow as if she no dey see clear. She still try chop after she born, but she find am hard to swallow the food. She continue to dey weak and she come dey feel dizzy too.

Wetin fit don happen? E fit be say she lose plenty blood during the delivery and now she need blood transfusion? Abi wetin suppose make we do for am? Should we give am food make she chop?
column19: The woman is experiencing postpartum hemorrhage, which is a common complication after childbirth. The first step is to ensure that the uterus is contracted to stop the bleeding. This can be done by massaging the abdomen and administering uterotonic drugs. If the bleeding does not stop, a blood transfusion may be necessary to replace the lost blood. It is also important to monitor the woman for signs of infection and provide supportive care.

**Wetin fit dey cause di bleeding:**
Di way she dey bleed plenty, wit pain, and say her last period na one month and two weeks ago, di main thing wey I go suspect na **miscarriage (abortion) or ectopic pregnancy** (belle wey enter tube instead of womb). Other causes fit be **incomplete miscarriage**, **molar pregnancy**, or **womb problem** like fibroid, but di history strong for pregnancy-related bleeding.

**Emergency things wey health workers suppose do sharp sharp:**
First, check her vital signs (BP, pulse, temperature) and see whether shock dey ("cold hand, fast pulse, low BP"). Open **two big IV lines** and start **IV fluids (Normal Saline or Ringer's Lactate)** quick quick to correct di blood wey she don lose. Collect blood for **grouping and cross-match** so dem fit give her blood transfusion if e need, and give oxygen if she dey breathe hard.

**Treatment and medicine wey fit save her life:**
If na incomplete miscarriage, give **IV/IM Oxytocin** or **Misoprostol** to help di womb contract and stop di bleeding, then do **manual vacuum aspiration (MVA) or evacuation** to comot anytin wey remain for inside womb. If na ectopic pregnancy wey don burst, she need **emergency surgery (laparotomy)** sharp sharp because dat one na life-and-death matter.

**Test wey suppose do:**
Do **urine pregnancy test (β-hCG)** first, **abdominal/transvaginal ultrasound** to know where di belle dey and if anytin remain for womb, **full blood count (PCV/haemoglobin)**, and **blood group with cross-match**. Dis go help know di real cause and guide di correct treatment to save her life.

**Wetin fit dey cause am:**
Di way hin heart dey beat fast, hand dey shake, and neck dey swell na sign say di woman fit get **hyperthyroidism** (tyroid gland dey work too much), and di common one for pregnancy na **Graves' disease**. Di neck swelling na **goiter** (di tyroid gland don big). E dey important make she see dr sharp sharp make dem check hin tyroid (TSH, T3, T4) and hin heart.

**How e fit affect di pikin:**
If dem no treat am well, e fit cause say di pikin no go grow well for belle, pikin fit born small (low birth weight), or di belle fit comot bifor time (miscarriage or premature birth). E fit also cause high blood pressure for di mama (pre-eclampsia) and problem for di pikin tyroid too.

**Danger sign wey dem suppose watch:**
Make dem run go hospital quick if di heart begin beat too too fast pass, chest dey pain, she dey find am hard to breathe, e get bad headache, eye dey blur, leg swell well well, or fever with confusion (dis one fit be **thyroid storm** wey dey very dangerous).

**Food and drink:**
Make she avoid too much **iodine** (like too much iodized salt, seaweed, and some cough medicine), and cut down **caffeine** (coffee, strong tea, energy drink) wey fit make heart beat fast pass. She suppose chop balanced food, plenty fruit, vegetable, protein and drink water well, but di main solution na make she see dr collect di correct medicine (like PTU for early pregnancy) wey safe for belle.

column19: Mama fit dey suffer from postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) or severe anemia because she carry heavy labor wey make her lose plenty blood. Di weakness, dizziness, and "eye no clear" na signs say her blood pressure fit low or her body no get enough blood to carry oxygen go her brain and muscles. You must quickly check her pulse, blood pressure, and check her urine color to see if she dey dehydrated or if she lose plenty blood. Instead of just giving her food, you must first give her IV fluids (like Ringers Lactate) and possibly a blood transfusion if her hemoglobin level low well-well. Make sure you also check her uterus to see if e still dey contract well, because if e no contract, e go continue to bleed inside.

As una dey go, keep pikin **sitting upright**, loosen tight cloth, clean nose gently if blocked, no give herbal mixture or force food/water if e dey choke.
If pikin stop breathing or turn blue, shout for help and rush go emergency sharp-sharp.

**Wetin fit cause am:** Serious lower belle pain wey join heavy bleeding for pregnancy fit be sign of these things: **miscarriage** (belle wan comot), **ectopic pregnancy** (belle wey grow for outside womb, especially for fallopian tube - dis one na emergency wey fit burst and cause plenty bleeding), **placental abruption** (di placenta comot from di womb before time), or **placenta previa** (placenta dey cover di mouth of di womb). If di belle never reach 20 weeks, na miscarriage or ectopic we dey suspect pass; if e don pass 20 weeks, na abruption or previa.

column18: As woman wey get mind wey dey hold her pikin when you see say the pikin body de hot the pikin body just begin to dey shake the pikin dey get convulsion and em no dey in control again Which kind sickness de do this pikin wey im mama still de give breast and which kind care dem fit give this pikin

**Wetin fit dey do the pikin:**

This pikin fit dey get **febrile convulsion** (fever wey dey cause the body to shake). Na common thing wey dey happen for pikin between 6 months to 5 years wia high fever dey make the body shake. But because the pikin body hot well-well and dey shake, we must also check for **malaria** (cerebral malaria), **meningitis**, or serious infection wey fit dey cause the fever.

**Care wey you fit give:**

1. **Put the pikin for im side** (make e no lie down for back) make saliva or vomit no block im throat, and no put anything for im mouth.
2. **Cool the body down** â remove cloth, use lukewarm water (no be cold water) rub the body, and give **paracetamol** to bring the fever down.
3. **Rush the pikin go hospital sharp-sharp** make dem check for malaria (do malaria test), check blood sugar, and rule out meningitis â the pikin fit need **artesunate** for malaria or antibiotics.
4. Mama fit continue **breastfeed** make the pikin no dey dehydrate, but if the pikin dey convulse, wait make e stop first.

Make you no waste time â carry the pikin go clinic quick-quick because convulsion wey no stop fit damage the brain.

**Wetin fit dey cause am:**

Dis pikin dey show sign of **neonatal hypothermia** wey don join with possible **neonatal sepsis** (serious infection). Di cold body, di way di pikin no gree suck breast, di weakness, di plenty sleep, and di poor movement/reflex na all danger signs wey dey show say dis na medical emergency. Di cold no be just because di pikin no dey suck—e fit be say infection or serious illness dey make di pikin body no fit keep body warm, and hypothermia self fit make di pikin weak and no gree suck (na cycle wey dey worsen).

**Treatment:**

1. **Warm di pikin sharp-sharp** with skin-to-skin (Kangaroo Mother Care)—put di pikin for mama chest, cover dem well with warm cloth and cap for head. Check di temperature.
2. **Refer/admit as emergency**—dis pikin need to enter hospital now-now for check-up, blood test, blood sugar (hypoglycaemia dey common), and **start antibiotics** for possible sepsis.
3. If di pikin no fit suck, dem fit give expressed breast milk through nasogastric tube (NG tube) or IV fluid, and check/treat low blood sugar.

**About di immunization:**

**No give di immunization today!** Immunization no dey give to sick pikin wey dey unstable like dis. Make dem first treat and stabilize di pikin, den give di vaccines when di pikin don recover well.

Abeg, make dem no waste time—dis one na emergency wey fit kill di pikin if dem delay.

# Wetin fit dey cause di bleeding (Secondary Postpartum Haemorrhage)

**Wetin fit cause am:** Di bleeding wey dey happen days after woman born (secondary PPH) fit be because **placenta piece remain for inside womb (retained products of conception)**, or **infection for inside womb (endometritis)**, or di **womb no fit contract well (uterine atony)**. Sometimes na wound wey dem sew (episiotomy or tear) wey open back.

**Treatment wey you go give:**
1. First, check her vital signs (BP, pulse) sharp-sharp, put drip (IV fluids) and take blood check her PCV/blood level.
2. Give **oxytocin or misoprostol** make di womb contract, and give **antibiotics** (like ampicillin + metronidazole) if infection dey.
3. If placenta piece still dey inside, dem go do **evacuation (D&C)**, and if her blood don low well-well, she fit need **blood transfusion**.

**Advice for mama and pikin:**
Make she chop well-well food wey get iron (like vegetable, meat, egg, beans), take her iron and folic acid tablets, rest well, and make she continue **breastfeeding** di pikin (breastfeeding sef dey help di womb contract). Make she come back sharp-sharp if di bleeding continue, if fever catch am, or if di blood smell bad.

Wetin dey happen to your husband fit really be **diabetes** (sugar sickness), because di plenty water drinking (polydipsia), plenty urine (polyuria), body tiredness, weight loss, and blurry vision na classic signs of high blood sugar. Di plenty thirst and urination na because di sugar dey too much for blood, so di body dey try comot am through urine, and dat one dey pull water comot di body, na why e dey always thirsty and tired. Fit be **Type 2 diabetes**, but at 40 years with weight loss, we go still check whether na Type 1 or even something like thyroid problem — na why test dey important.

**Di test wey e need do:** Make e go hospital sharp-sharp make dem check **fasting blood sugar (FBS)**, **random blood sugar**, and **HbA1c** (wey dey show average sugar for 3 months), plus **urine test** to check sugar and ketones — no dey delay dis test o. Na di doctor go confirm am and start treatment, and if na diabetes, e go need see doctor regularly, no be only one time.

**Food and lifestyle:** Make e avoid sugary drinks (minerals, sweet juice), too much white rice, bread, and sugary things; make e chop plenty vegetables, beans, whole grains, and small portion of food, plus drink water and do exercise like waka-waka. If e dey feel dizzy when e stand up, make e stand slowly, but e need reach hospital quick-quick because if di sugar too high e fit enter emergency — no waste time, carry am go clinic today.

**Wetin fit cause am:** Di pikin dey show sign of **birth asphyxia** (wey mean say oxygen no reach di pikin brain well during delivery), wey fit cause **Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE)**. Odda tins wey fit cause dis kind sign na **neonatal sepsis** (infection), **hypoglycaemia** (sugar low), or **neonatal jaundice** wey don enter brain (kernicterus).

**Test wey dem fit do:** Check di pikin **blood sugar (RBS)** sharp-sharp, **SpO2** (oxygen level), **full blood count** and **blood culture** to find infection, **serum bilirubin** if di pikin yellow, and if e possible do **cranial ultrasound** or **EEG** to check di brain.

**Emergency step:** Follow **neonatal resuscitation (HBB – Helping Babies Breathe)** — dry di pikin, keep am warm, clear di airway, and if e no dey breathe well, use **bag and mask to ventilate** with oxygen. Correct any low sugar with **IV dextrose (10%)**, and refer sharp-sharp go where dem get **NICU** if e dey serious.

**Treatment:** Give **oxygen support**, IV fluid and antibiotics (like **ampicillin + gentamicin**) if sepsis dey suspected, control any convulsion with **phenobarbitone**, and where e dey available, **therapeutic hypothermia (cooling)** dey help pikin wey get HIE if dem start am within 6 hours after birth.

# Wetin Fit Dey Wrong With Di Pikin

Di way you describe am, di pikin fit get **birth asphyxia** (wey mean say oxygen no reach di pikin brain well during delivery) - dis one dey cause **HIE (Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy)**, wey dey make pikin no cry, no move well, and body dey stiff or floppy. Odda things wey fit cause am na **infection/sepsis, low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), meningitis, or brain problem** wey pikin born with.

## Wetin Health Worker Suppose Do Sharp-Sharp (Resuscitation Steps)

Follow di **Helping Babies Breathe** steps: **dry di pikin, keep am warm, clean di mouth and nose, and rub di back to help am breathe.** If pikin still no dey breathe within **one minute (di Golden Minute)**, start **bag and mask ventilation** to push air enter di pikin lungs, and make sure di airway open well.

Give **oxygen**, check and correct **blood sugar**, and start **antibiotics** (like Ampicillin and Gentamicin) if dem suspect infection. Make dem **refer di pikin quick-quick go bigger hospital** wey get **NICU (special baby care unit)** for further care, and control **seizures** if e dey happen with medicine like Phenobarbital.
